 Order

Dated this the 30th day of March, 2026 The sole accused in S.C. No. 856 of 2023 on the file of the Additional Sessions Court (Violence against Women and Children), Ernakulam, arising out of Crime No. 411 of 2022 of Kalamassery police station, has filed this Crl.M.C. under Section 528 of the B.N.S.S., praying for quashing all further proceedings against him.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Court (Violence against Women and Children), Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offence alleged against the petitioner is under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC.

2. The prosecution case is that the accused, after promising to marry the defacto complainant,
committed rape upon her repeatedly during the period from October 2019 till September 2020.
3.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, even if the entire allegations levelled against the petitioner are believed as such, the same do not constitute the offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC.
Therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
CRL.MC NO. 173 OF 2026 2026:KER:28915 Radhakrishnan vs State Of Kerala on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161759143/
2 4. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent/defacto complainant as well as by the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. On a perusal of the FI statement, it can be seen that the defacto complainant was aged 48 at the time of the alleged incident and she was a divorcee and mother of two children aged 28 and 24.

It appears that, while so, she and the petitioner became friends and as invited by the petitioner she went to the flat of the petitioner at Kalamassery during night and stayed along with him overnight.
The first incident of alleged rape occurred during the said night.
Though it appears that the above incident was without the consent of the defacto complainant, their relationship continued for a considerable period from October 2019 till September 2020.

From the subsequent conduct of the defacto complainant in permitting the petitioner to have sexual intercourse with her for a considerable period, it can be seen that the relationship between them was a consensual one.
There is absolutely nothing to show that the defacto complainant had given consent because of misconception of any CRL.MC NO. 173 OF 2026 2026:KER:28915 facts.

Therefore, the allegations levelled against the petitioner do not make out the offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC and as such there is no meaning in continuing the proceedings against the petitioner.
Therefore, this Crl.M.C. is liable to be allowed.
In the result, this Crl.M.C. is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioner in S.C. No. 856 of 2023 on the file of the Additional Sessions Court (Violence against women and children),
Ernakulam, arising out of Crime No. 411 of 2022 of Kalamassery police station, is quashed.
